summary: Document the Atlas lean launch and introduce deterministic feature-review governance without changing runtime product behaviour.

preservation.evidence: No application behaviour, schemas, dependencies or existing product gates changed. The previous baseline audit is retained and linked.

customer.evidence: This PR documents the customer journey only; no customer routes, UI or response serializers were changed.

planner.evidence: This PR documents the planner journey only; no planner routes, UI or planning algorithms were changed.

flagsOnOff.evidence: Registry is explicitly design-only and runtimeStatus is planned for every group. No operational flag switching is claimed or enabled.

authorization.evidence: No product access control changed. CI token permissions are limited to contents read. Required remote human approval and protected governance are documented, not configured.

integrations.evidence: No provider calls, credentials, callbacks or service configuration changed. Future adapter properties and failure handling are documented.

migrationRollback.evidence: No schema or data migration. Revert the documentation and CI commit to restore prior repository governance without touching application data.

validation.evidence: Executed node scripts/check-feature-review.mjs, node --test scripts/check-feature-review.test.mjs (9 passed), and git diff --check. CLI fixture rejects missing evidence and accepts a completed record.

documentation.evidence: Lean launch plan, pre-merge prompt, registry, root development instructions, PR template and historical-plan links updated together. Runtime implementation and remote-enforcement limits are explicit.
